label: def_pseudoconcave
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def_pseudoconcave}
For a function $\phi:\mathbb{R}_+ \left( := \left(0, \infty \right) \right)  \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_+$, we define 
$$
s_\phi(\lambda) := \sup_{t>0}\frac{\phi(\lambda t)}{\phi(t)}\,,
$$
so that $s_{\phi}:\mathbb{R}_+\rightarrow (0,\infty]$.
Observe that $s_\phi$ is \textit{submultiplicative}, \textit{i.e}., $s_\phi(\lambda\tau) \leq s_\phi(\lambda) s_\phi(\tau)$ for $\lambda, \tau>0$.
Together with the definition of $s_\phi(\lambda)$, we introduce the following class of functions.
For $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a \le b$, we set
	\begin{align}\label{ftn class}
		\mathcal{I}(a, b) := \{\phi : \textrm{$s_\phi(\lambda) = O(\lambda^a)$ as $\lambda \to 0$, and $s_\phi(\lambda) = O(\lambda^b)$ as $\lambda \to \infty$} \}.
	\end{align}
We also define $\mathcal{I}_o(a,b)$, where $o$ denotes that we replace $O$-notation with $o$-notation in \eqref{ftn class}. Clearly, $\mathcal{I}_o(a,b)\subsetneq \mathcal{I}(a,b)$.

title: Definition
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item     For $p\in(1,\infty)$, let $A_p=A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be the class of all nonnegative and locally integrable functions $w$ satisfying
\begin{align}
\label{def ap}
[w]_{A_p}:=\sup_{\mathcal{Q}\,\text{cubes in }\mathbb{R}^d}\left(-\hspace{-0.40cm}\int_{\mathcal{Q}}w(x)dx\right)\left(-\hspace{-0.40cm}\int_{\mathcal{Q}}w(x)^{-1/(p-1)}dx\right)^{p-1}<\infty.
\end{align}
The class of $A_1=A_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is defined as a collection of nonnegative and locally integrable functions $w$ satisfying
$$
\mathcal{M} w(x)\leq Cw(x) \quad \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
$$
where $\mathcal{M}$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator and $C$ is independent of $x$.
The class $A_{\infty}=A_{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ could be defined as the union of $A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for all $p\in[1,\infty)$, \textit{i.e.},
    $$
    A_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)=\bigcup_{p\in[1,\infty)}A_p(\mathbb{R}^d).
    $$
\item For $s\in(1,\infty)$, let $RH_s=RH_s(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be the class of all nonnegative and locally integrable functions $w$ satisfying
$$
[w]_{RH_{s}}:=\sup_{\mathcal{Q}\,\text{cubes in }\mathbb{R}^d}\left(-\hspace{-0.40cm}\int_{\mathcal{Q}}w(x)^s\mathrm{d}x\right)^{1/s}\left(-\hspace{-0.40cm}\int_{\mathcal{Q}}w(x)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{-1} < \infty.
$$
The class of $RH_{\infty}=RH_{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is defined as a collection of nonnegative and locally integrable functions $w$ satisfying
$$
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\in \mathcal{Q}}w(x)\leq C-\hspace{-0.40cm}\int_{\mathcal{Q}}w(x)\mathrm{d}x
$$
for all cubes $\mathcal{Q}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. Here, $C$ is independent of $\mathcal{Q}$.
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{def_diff}
	Let $p\in(1,\infty]$, $q\in[1,\infty]$, $M>0$, $\phi\in \mathcal{I}_o(0,M)$, and denote by $L$ the smallest integer not less than $M$.
If $p<\infty$, then we set $w\in A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and if $p=\infty$, then we set $L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x):=L_{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. 
For a given function $f$, let $\mathcal{D}_h^1 f (x) = \mathcal{D}_h f (x) = f(x+h) - f(x)$ and $\mathcal{D}_h^L = \mathcal{D}_h \mathcal{D}_h^{L-1}$ for $L = 2, 3, \cdots$.

    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item
    The space $\mathcal{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)$ is defined by
    $$
    \mathcal{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x):=\{f\in\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d):\|f\|_{\mathcal{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}<\infty\},
    $$
    where $\|f\|_{\mathcal{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}$ is given by
    \begin{eqnarray}\label{wBesov_norm_diff}
    \|f\|_{\mathcal{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}:=\|f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}
    +\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d} x)},
    \end{eqnarray}
    and $\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}$ is also given by
    $$
    \|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d} x)}:=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} \Big(\int_{|h|\leq 1} \phi(|h|^{-1})^q  \left\| \mathcal{D}_h^L f \right\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)}^q~\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{|h|^d}\Big)^{1/q}, &q<\infty,\\
    \sup_{|h|\leq 1}\phi(|h|^{-1}) \left\| \mathcal{D}_h^L f \right\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)},&q=\infty.
    \end{array}
    \right.
    $$
    We also define the space $\mathscr{B}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)$ together with a norm given by \eqref{wBesov_norm_diff} with $\mathbb{R}^d$ instead of $|h|\leq 1$.
    \item
    The space $\mathcal{F}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)$ is defined by
    $$
    \mathcal{F}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x):=\{f\in\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d):\|f\|_{\mathcal{F}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}<\infty\},
    $$
    where $\|f\|_{\mathcal{F}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}$ is given by
    \begin{eqnarray}\label{wTL_norm_diff}
    \|f\|_{\mathcal{F}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}:=\|f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}
    +\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d} x)},
    \end{eqnarray}
    and $\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}$ is also given by
    $$
    \|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}:=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}\Big\| \Big(\int_{|h|\leq 1} \phi(|h|^{-1})^q   |\mathcal{D}_h^L f|^q~\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{|h|^d}\Big)^{1/q} \Big\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)}, &q<\infty,\\
    \Big\| \sup_{|h|\leq 1}\phi(|h|^{-1}) |\mathcal{D}_h^L f| \Big\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)},&q=\infty.
    \end{array}
    \right.
    $$
    Similarly, we define the space $\mathscr{F}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x)$ together with the norm given by \eqref{wTL_norm_diff} with $\mathbb{R}^d$ instead of $|h|\leq 1$.
    \end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm_lp_diff_equiv}
Let $w \in A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $p \in (1, \infty]$, and we assume that
$$
M > \frac{d}{p}\left(R_w + \frac{1}{\Gamma_w} - 1\right).
$$ 
	Then 
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item for $p\in(1,\infty]$, $q\in[1,\infty]$ and $\phi\in\mathcal{I}_o \left(\frac{d}{p}\left(R_w+\frac{1}{\Gamma_w}-1\right),M \right)$,
 $$
 B_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w~\mathrm{d}x)=\mathcal{B}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w~\mathrm{d}x)=\mathscr{B}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x).
 $$
	\item for $p,q\in(1, \infty)$ and $\phi\in\mathcal{I}_o(\frac{dR_{w}}{p},M)$,
 $$
 F_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w~\mathrm{d}x)=\mathcal{F}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w~\mathrm{d}x)=\mathscr{F}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d, w\,\mathrm{d}x).
 $$
 \end{enumerate}
 Here, the constants $R_w$ and $\Gamma_w$ are defined by
 $$
 R_w:=\inf\{q:w\in A_q(\mathbb{R}^d)\}\in[1,p],\quad \Gamma_w:=\sup\{s:w\in RH_s(\mathbb{R}^d)\}\in[1,\infty].
 $$

body_md:
\label{23.04.21.16.12}
Let $p,s\in(1,\infty)$, $\mathcal{Q}$ be a cube and $S\subset \mathcal{Q}$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item If $w\in A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then $w\in A_q(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $q<p$.
    \item If $w\in A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then 
    $$
    \left(\frac{|S|}{|\mathcal{Q}|}\right)^p \leq [w]_{A_p}\frac{w(S)}{w(\mathcal{Q})}\,.
    $$
    \item If $w\in A_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then there exists a constant $s=s(d,p,[w]_{A_p})>1$ such that $w\in RH_{s}(\mathbb{R}^d)$
    \item If $w\in RH_s(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then $w\in RH_{t}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $t>s$.
    \item If $w\in RH_s(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then
    $$
    \frac{w(S)}{w(\mathcal{Q})}\leq [w]_{RH_s}\left(\frac{|S|}{|\mathcal{Q}|}\right)^{1-1/s} \,.
    $$
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item 
            This is an easy consequence of \cite[Theorem 1.3.1-1]{triebel1983theory} with the fact that $(1+|z|)^{d/r}\simeq 1+|z|^{d/r}$.
        
        \item
            By an almost orthogonality of $\Delta_j$,
            \begin{align*}
                |D^{\alpha}_{x}\Delta_jf(x)|&\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|\Delta_jf(x-y)|\sum_{k=-1}^1|D^{\alpha}_{x}\psi_{2^{j+k}}(y)|~\mathrm{d}y \\
                &\leq M_{j,\lambda}^{*}f(x)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+2^j|y|)^{\lambda}\sum_{k=-1}^1|D^{\alpha}_{x}\psi_{2^{j+k}}(y)|~\mathrm{d}y.
            \end{align*}
            Clearly,
            $$
            	\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+2^j|y|)^{\lambda}\sum_{k=-1}^1|D^{\alpha}_{x}\psi_{2^{j+k}}(y)|~\mathrm{d}y=:c2^{j|\alpha|},
            $$
            and we remark that $c$ is independent of $j$. 
            Similarly,
            $$
            	|D^{\alpha}_{x}S_0f(x)|\leq M_{\lambda}^{0,*}f(x).
            $$
        
        \item 
            Let $g_j(x):=\Delta_jf(2^{-j}x)$. Then
            $$
            	\widehat{g_j}(\xi):=2^{jd}\widehat{\psi}(\xi)\widehat{f}(2^j\xi),\quad \widehat{S_0f}(\xi):=\widehat{\Phi}(\xi)\widehat{f}(\xi).
            $$
            Thus $\mathrm{supp}(\widehat{g_j}),\mathrm{supp}(\widehat{S_0f})\subseteq B_2(0)$. 
            Then by the first assertion,
            \begin{align*}
                \sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|g_j(x-z)|}{(1+|z|)^{d/r}} &\leq N(\mathcal{M}(|g_j|^r)(x))^{1/r},\\
                \sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|S_0f(x-z)|}{(1+|z|)^{d/r}} &=M_{\lambda}^{0,*}f(x) \leq N(\mathcal{M}(|S_0f|^r)(x))^{1/r}.
            \end{align*}
            This implies that
            \begin{align*}
                M_{j,d/r}^{*}f(2^{-j}x)&=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|\Delta_jf(2^{-j}x-z)|}{(1+2^{j}|z|)^{d/r}}=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|\Delta_jf(2^{-j}x-2^{-j}z)|}{(1+|z|)^{d/r}}\\
                &=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|g_j(x-z)|}{(1+|z|)^{d/r}}\\
                &\leq N(\mathcal{M}(|g_j|^r)(x))^{1/r}=N(\mathcal{M}(|\Delta_jf|^r)(2^{-j}x))^{1/r}.
            \end{align*}
        
        \item 
          	Due to \eqref{230610943} and the definition of $\mathcal{D}_\rho^L$, we have
            $$
            	|\mathcal{D}_{\rho}^L\Delta_jf(x)|\leq \min\Big(|\rho|^{L}\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}\sum_{|\alpha|=L}|D^{\alpha}_{x}\Delta_jf(x-z)|,\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}|\Delta_jf(x-z)|\Big).
            $$
            By the second assertion of the lemma, 
            $$
            	|\mathcal{D}_{\rho}^L\Delta_jf(x)|\leq N\min(1,|\rho|2^{j})^L\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}M_{j,\lambda}^{*}f(x-z).
            $$
            Since
            $$
            	\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}M_{j,\lambda}^{*}f(x-z)\leq N(1+2^{j}|\rho|)^{\lambda}M_{j,\lambda}^{*}f(x),
            $$
            we obtain the result. 
            Similarly,
            $$
            	|\mathcal{D}_{\rho}^{L}S_0f(x)|\leq N\min(1,|\rho|)^L\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}M_{\lambda}^{0,*}f(x-z)
            $$
            and
            $$
            	\sup_{|z|\leq L|\rho|}M_{\lambda}^{0,*}f(x-z)\leq N(1+|\rho|)^{\lambda}M_{\lambda}^{0,*}f(x).
            $$
        
        \item 
            Note that $\Phi$ from \eqref{ineq_230315_1246} is in $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, hence it follows that
            \begin{align*}
            	|S_0f(x)|
		\leq &\int_{B_{1}(0)}|f(x-y)\Phi(y)|~\mathrm{d}y\\
		 &+\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\int_{B_{2^k}(0)\setminus\overline{B_{2^{k-1}}(0)}}|f(x-y)\Phi(y)|~\mathrm{d}y
            \end{align*}
            and
            $$
            	|\Phi(y)|+|y|^{d+1}|\Phi(y)|\leq N.
            $$
            This certainly implies that $|S_0f|\leq N\mathcal{M} f$. For $\Delta_j$, the change of variable formula yields
            $$
            	\Delta_jf(x)
		=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}f(x-y)\psi_{2^j}(y)~\mathrm{d}y
		=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}f(x-2^{-j}y)\psi(y)~\mathrm{d}y.
            $$
            Using the similar arguments, we have $|\Delta_jf(x)|\leq N\mathcal{M} f(x)$. The lemma is proved.
    \end{enumerate}

title: Definition
body_md:
An operator $T:L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)\to L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)$ is linearizable if there exist a Banach space $B$ and a $B$-valued linear operator $U:L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)\to L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x;B)$ such that
    $$
    	|Tf(x)| = \| Uf(x)\|_B,\quad \forall f\in L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x).
    $$

title: Proof
body_md:
One can observe that $f=S_0f+\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\Delta_jf$.
    By Minkowski's inequality,
    $$
    	\|f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\leq \|S_0f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}+\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}.
    $$
    By \eqref{w scaling}, we have
    \begin{equation}
    \label{23.01.29.17.13}
        2^{\varepsilon j}\lesssim\frac{\phi(2^j)}{\phi(1)},
    \end{equation}
    which clearly implies that  $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^{-1}\lesssim \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}2^{-\varepsilon j}<\infty$.
    Hence
    $$
    \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^{-1}\phi(2^j)\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\lesssim \sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^j)\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}.
    $$
    Therefore, $\|f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\leq N\|f\|_{B_{p,\infty}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}$.
    For the case $q \in [1, \infty)$, it directly follows that
    \begin{align*}
    &\sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^j)\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\\
    \leq&\max\left(\left(\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}^q\right)^{1/q},\left\|\left(\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q|\Delta_jf|^q\right)^{1/q}\right\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\right).
    \end{align*}
    and therefore,
    $$
    	\|f\|_{L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}\leq N\min(\|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)},\|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}).
    $$
The lemma is proved.

label: ineq_230504_1659
title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that 
\begin{align*}
	B_0 &= \|f\|_{L_p(w)} + \Big\| \{ \phi(2^j)^q\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(w)}^q \}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \Big\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})},\\
	F_0 &= \|f\|_{L_p(w)} + \Big\| \| \{ \phi(2^j)^q \left| \Delta_jf \right|^q\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})} \Big\|_{L_p(w)},
\end{align*}
when $q\geq1$ including $q=\infty$.
Since $| S_0f (x) |\leq N\mathcal{M}(f)(x)$, one immediately obtains
$$
\|f\|_{X_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}\lesssim X_0.
$$
For the converse inequality, observe that
\begin{align}
	\|f\|_{L_p(w)} &\leq  \|S_0f\|_{L_p(w)}+ A_{q'}\Big\| \{\phi(2^j) \|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(w)}\}_{j\geq1} \Big\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})},\label{ineq_230504_1659}\\
	\|f\|_{L_p(w)} &\leq  \|S_0f\|_{L_p(w)}+ A_{q'}\Big\| \| \{\phi(2^j) |\Delta_jf|\}_{j\geq1} \|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})} \Big\|_{L_p(w)},\label{ineq_230504_1700}
\end{align}
where$A_{q'} = (\sum_{j\geq1} \phi(2^j)^{-q'})^{1/q'}$, which is bounded by $(\sum_{j\geq1} 2^{-j\varepsilon q'})^{1/q'}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$.
Note that we have $\|f\|_{L_p(w)} \lesssim \|f\|_{X_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}$ by \eqref{ineq_230504_1659} and \eqref{ineq_230504_1700}.
Thus it suffices to handle the following terms:
$$
	\Big\| \{ \phi(2^j)^q\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(w)}^q \}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \Big\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})},\quad \Big\| \| \{ \phi(2^j)^q \left| \Delta_jf \right|^q\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z})} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}.
$$
We only consider $j\leq 0$ parts, since $j\geq1$ parts are already contained in $\|f\|_{X_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}$.

When $X=B$, we make use of
$$
	\Delta_jf=\Delta_j(S_0+\Delta_1)f \quad \forall j=0,-1,-2,\cdots.
$$
Then together with $\phi(2^j) \lesssim 2^{j(M- \varepsilon)}$, we have for $q\in[1,\infty]$
\begin{align*}
	\Big\| \| \{ \phi(2^j)^q\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p(w)}\}_{j\leq 0} \Big\|_{\ell^q}
	&\lesssim \| \{ 2^{j(M-\varepsilon)} \}_{j\leq1} \|_{\ell^q} \sup_{j\leq 0}\| \Delta_j f\|_{L_p(w)}\\
	&\lesssim \|S_0f\|_{L_p(w)}+\|\Delta_1f\|_{L_p(w)}.
\end{align*}
This certainly implies that
$$
	X_0 \lesssim \|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}.
$$

When $X=F$, we apply Lemma~\ref{23.01.31.17.22}.
Let $T_j:=\Delta_j$ and $f_j:=\phi(2^j)f$ in Lemma~\ref{23.01.31.17.22}. 
Since $|\Delta_jf(x)|\leq N\mathcal{M}(f)(x)$, one verifies that $\{T_j\}_{j\leq0}$ is linearizable and satisfies \eqref{22.09.13.16.42}. 
Then by Lemma \ref{23.01.31.17.22}, it follows that
\begin{align*}
	\Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\leq 0} \phi(2^j)^q \left| \Delta_jf \right|^q\Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}
	&=\Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\leq 0} \left| T_jf_j\right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}\\
	&\lesssim \Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\leq 0} \left| f_j \right|^q\Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}
	\lesssim \|f\|_{L_p(w)},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from $\phi(2^j)\lesssim 2^{j(M - \varepsilon)}$.
The lemma is proved.

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that 
\begin{align*}
	B_1 &= \inf\Big(\|f\|_{L_p(w)} + \Big(\sum_{j\geq0} \phi(2^j)^q \|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}\Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big),\\
	F_1 &=  \inf\Big(\|f\|_{L_p(w)} + \Big\| \Big(\sum_{j\geq0} \phi(2^j)^q |f-f_j|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big) \Big\|_{L_p(w)},
\end{align*}
where the infimum runs over all sequences of functions $\{f_j\}_{j\geq0} \subset \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L_p(w)$ such that
$$
	f = \lim_{j\to\infty}f_j\,\,\text{in}\,\, \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d), \quad \text{and}\quad \mathrm{supp}(\widehat{f}_j) \subset B_{2^{j+1}}(0).
$$

\textbf{Step 1.} $X_1 \lesssim\|f\|_{X_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}$.

In this step, by the similarity, we only prove for $X=B$.
From the support condition of $\widehat{f_j}$, we have
$$
	f_j:=S_0f+\sum_{k=1}^{j}\Delta_kf,\quad f_0:=S_0f,
$$
and
$$
	f-f_j=\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}\Delta_kf,
$$
Then by Minkowski's inequality, it follows that 
$$
	\|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}\leq \sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}.
$$
For $q\in[1,\infty)$, we apply H\"older's inequality to obtain
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}^q
    &\leq \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\left(\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}\right)^{q}\\
    &\leq N\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}2^{q\delta(k-j-1)}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^{q}\\
    &\leq N\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(k-j-1)}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^{q},
\end{align*}
where $\delta=0$ if $q=1$ and $\delta>0$ if $q\in(1,\infty)$. If we choose $\varepsilon>\delta\geq0$ and use Fubini's theorem, then
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(k-j-1)}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^{q}
    &=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\phi(2^k)^q2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(k-j-1)}\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^{q}\\
    &\leq N\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^{q}\leq N\|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}^q.
\end{align*}
For $q=\infty$, we simply have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{gathered}
	\phi(2^j)\|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}
	\leq N\sum_{k=j+1}^{\infty}2^{\varepsilon(j-k)}\phi(2^k)\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}
	\leq N\sup_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^k)\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation*}
This implies that
$$
	B_1 \leq N\|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}.
$$




\textbf{Step 2.} $\|f\|_{X_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}\lesssim X_1$.


First we consider $X=B$. Similar to the previous case, for $k\geq2$ one can observe that
$$
	\Delta_kf=\sum_{j=-1}^{\infty}\Delta_k(f_{k+j}-f_{k+j-1}).
$$
Since $\Delta_j f$ is less than a constant multiple of $\mathcal{M} f$, we use the weighted $L_p$ boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function so that
\begin{align*}
    \|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}\leq N\sum_{j=k-1}^{\infty}\|f_{j}-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}.
\end{align*}
Take $\delta=0$ if $q=1$ and $\delta>0$ if $q\in(1,\infty)$. 
For $q\in[1,\infty)$, we apply H\"older's inequality and Fubini's theorem to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{ineq_230316_1512}
\begin{aligned}
    \sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}^q
    &\leq N\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q\sum_{j=k-1}^{\infty}2^{q\delta(j-k)}\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}^q\\
    &\leq N\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\sum_{j=k-1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(j-k)}\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}^q\\
    &=N\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=2}^{j+1}\phi(2^j)^q2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(j-k)}\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}^q\\
    &=N\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}^q,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where $\varepsilon>\delta\geq0$. 
For $q=\infty$, we simply have
$$
	\phi(2^k)\|\Delta_kf\|_{L_p(w)}\leq N\sum_{j=k-1}^{\infty}2^{\varepsilon(k-j)}\phi(2^j)\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}\leq N\sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^j)\|f_j-f_{j-1}\|_{L_p(w)}.
$$

It is left to control $\|S_0 f\|_{L_p(w)}$ and $\|\Delta_j f\|_{L_p(w)}$.
One can observe that
\begin{align*}
    \|S_0f\|_{L_p(w)}+\|\Delta_1f\|_{L_p(w)}
    &\leq N\|f\|_{L_p(w)}
    	\leq N\|f_0\|_{L_p(w)}+\|f-f_0\|_{L_p(w)}\\
    &\lesssim \|f_0\|_{L_p(w)}+\Big( \sum_{j=0}^\infty \phi(2^j)^q \|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}}.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
    \|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}&\lesssim \|f_0\|_{L_p(w)}+\Big( \sum_{j=0}^\infty \phi(2^j)^q \|f-f_j\|_{L_p(w)}^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}}
\end{align*}
for all sequences of functions $\{f_j\}_{j=0}^{\infty}$ and this certainly implies that
$$
	\|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}\lesssim X_1.
$$

Now, we suppose $X=F$. 
Similar to \eqref{ineq_230316_1512}, for $q\in(1,\infty)$ we have
$$
	\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\phi(2^k)^q|\Delta_kf|^q\leq N\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\sum_{k=2}^{j+1}2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(j-k)}|\Delta_k(f_j-f_{j-1})|^q.
$$
Then $|\Delta_k(f_j-f_{j-1})|\leq N\mathcal{M}(f_j-f_{j-1})$ yields 
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\sum_{k=2}^{j+1}2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(j-k)}|\Delta_k(f_j-f_{j-1})|^q
    &\leq N\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q|\mathcal{M}(f_j-f_{j-1})|^q\sum_{k=2}^{j+1}2^{q(\delta-\varepsilon)(j-k)}\\
    &= N\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q|\mathcal{M}(f_j-f_{j-1})|^q.
\end{align*}
Let $T_j:=\mathcal{M}$ and $G_j:=\phi(2^j)(f_j-f_{j-1})$ in Lemma~\ref{23.01.31.17.22}. 
Note that $\{T_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ is linearizable and satisfies \eqref{22.09.13.16.42}. 
Thus by Lemma \ref{23.01.31.17.22}, it follows that
\begin{align*}
    \Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\geq 1} \phi(2^j)^q \left| \mathcal{M}(f_j-f_{j-1}) \right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}
    &=\Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\geq 1}  \left| T_j G_j \right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}\\
    &\lesssim \Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\geq 1}  \left| G_j \right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}\\
    &=  \Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\geq 1} \phi(2^j)^q \left| f_j - f_{j-1} \right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)}
\end{align*}
Hence
\begin{align*}
    \|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}&\leq \|S_0f\|_{L_p(w)}+\Big\| \Big( \sum_{j\geq 1} \phi(2^j)^q \left| f_j - f_{j-1} \right|^q \Big)^{\frac{1}{q}} \Big\|_{L_p(w)},
\end{align*}
for all sequences of functions $\{f_j\}_{j=0}^{\infty}$ and this certainly implies that
$
	\|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}\lesssim F_1.
$
The lemma is proved.

body_md:
By similarity, we only provide proof for the homogeneous Besov case.
It directly follows from the proof of Lemmas~\ref{23.02.08.15.54} and \ref{23.02.08.15.55} that
$$
\|f\|_{\mathring{B}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d} x)}^q\simeq  \int_0^\infty \phi(t^{-1})^q \left\| \psi_{\frac{1}{t}} \ast f \right\|_{L_p(w)}^q ~\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\simeq  \int_0^\infty \phi(t^{-1})^q \left\| \psi^L_{\frac{1}{t}} \ast f \right\|_{L_p(w)}^q ~\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\,,
$$
where $\psi_{1/t}^L$ is the function defined in \eqref{2307101129}.
Due to the proof of \eqref{230611958}, we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_0^\infty \phi(t^{-1})^q \left\| \psi^L_{\frac{1}{t}} \ast f \right\|_{L_p(w)}^q ~\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\,&\lesssim \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\bigg(\int_{0}^{\infty}\phi(t^{-1})^q|\psi_{1/t}(y)|\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\bigg)\big\|\mathcal{D}_y^Lf\big\|_{L_p(w)}^q\,\mathrm{d} y\\
&\lesssim \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(|y|^{-1})^q\big\|\mathcal{D}_y^Lf\big\|_{L_p(w)}^q\frac{\,\mathrm{d} y}{|y|^d}=\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d} x)}^q.
\end{align*}
Therefore, the estimate
$\|f\|_{\mathring{B}_{p,q}^\phi(w)}\lesssim \|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(w)}$
is obtained.
Due to \eqref{2307101154}, 
$$
\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_0}\lesssim \|f\|_{\mathring{B}_{p,q}^\phi(w)}\,,
$$
where 
$$
\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_0}:=
\begin{cases}
    \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(|h|^{-1})^q\sup_{|\rho|\leq|h|}\|\mathcal{D}^L_{\rho}f\|_{L_p(w)}^q\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{|h|^d}\right)^{1/q},\quad &q<\infty,\\
    \sup_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(|h|^{-1})\sup_{|\rho|\leq|h|}\|\mathcal{D}^L_{\rho}f\|_{L_p(w)},\quad &q=\infty.
\end{cases}
$$
Since
$$
\|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(w)}\lesssim \|f\|_{\mathring{\mathcal{B}}_0},
$$
we also have the converse estimate.
The theorem is proved.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first observe that for any multi-index $\alpha\in\big(\mathbb{N}_0\big)^d$ and $x,\,h\in\mathbb{R}^d$, 
\begin{align}\label{230714604}
\mathcal{D}^L_h(x^\alpha):=\sum_{k=0}^{L}\binom{L}{k}(-1)^{L-k}(x+kh)^\alpha=
\begin{cases}
0 &\text{if}\quad |\alpha|< L\\[2mm]
\sum\limits_{\substack{\beta:L\leq |\beta|,\,\beta\leq \alpha}}c_{\alpha,\beta}x^{\alpha-\beta}h^\beta &\text{if}\quad |\alpha|\geq L\,,
\end{cases}
\end{align}
for some nonzero constants $c_{\alpha,\beta}$.
Here, for $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)$ and $\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_d)$, $\beta\leq \alpha$ denotes that $\beta_i\leq \alpha_i$ for all $i=1,\,\ldots,\,d$.
Indeed,
$$
\mathcal{D}_h^L(x^\alpha)=\sum_{\beta:\beta\leq \alpha}\left(\sum_{k=0}^L\binom{L}{k}(-1)^{L-k}k^{|\beta|}\right)\binom{\alpha}{\beta}x^{\alpha-\beta}h^\beta,\quad \text{where}\,\,\,\,\binom{\alpha}{\beta}:=\prod_{i=1}^d\binom{\alpha_i}{\beta_i}\,,
$$
and
\begin{align*}
\sum_{k=0}^L\binom{L}{k}(-1)^{L-k}k^{n}=\left[\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^n\left(\mathrm{e}^t-1\right)^L\right]_{t=0}=
\begin{cases}
    0 &\text{if}\quad n<L\\[2mm]
    \text{positive constant}&\text{if}\quad n\geq L\,.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
It follows from \eqref{230714604} that if $P$ is a polynomial with $\mathrm{deg}\,P<L$, then $\mathcal{D}_h^LP\equiv 0$ for all $h\in\mathbb{R}^d$, which implies the first assertion in \eqref{230714638}.
For the second assertion in \eqref{230714638}, due to similarity, we consider only the case $\mathring{\mathscr{X}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d)=\mathring{\mathscr{B}}_{p,q}^\phi(\mathbb{R}^d)$.
Let $\mathrm{deg}\,P=:M\geq L$, then \eqref{230714604} implies that
$$
\mathcal{D}_h^LP(x)=\sum_{i=L}^{M}Q_i(x,h)
$$
where $Q_i(x,h)$ is a polynomial satisfying that
$$
Q_i(x,h)=|h|^iQ_i\big(x,h/|h|\big)\quad\forall\,\, x,\,h\in\mathbb{R}^d\qquad ;\qquad Q_M\not\equiv 0\,.
$$
Take $(x_0,\sigma_0)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ and $\delta>0$ such that
$$
\inf_{(x,\sigma)\in E_1\times E_2 }|Q_M(x,\sigma)|=:2\epsilon_0>0\,,
$$
where $E_1=B_\delta(x_0)$ and $E_2=B_\delta(\sigma_0)\cap \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$.
Put 
$$
N_0=\sup_{(x,\sigma)\in E_1\times E_2}\sum_{i=L}^{M-1}|Q_i(x,\sigma)|\quad\text{and}\quad R=:\frac{N_0}{\epsilon_0}\vee 1\,.
$$
Then for any $x\in E_1$, $\sigma\in E_2$, and $r\geq R$,
$$
|\mathcal{D}_{r\sigma}^{L}P(x)|\geq r^M|Q_M(x,\sigma)|-\sum_{i=L}^{M-1}r^i|Q_i(x,\sigma)|\geq r^{M}\bigg(2\epsilon_0-\frac{N_0}{R}\bigg)\geq \epsilon_0 r^M\,.
$$
Consequently, we obtain that 
\begin{equation}\label{230714725}
\begin{aligned}
\|P\|_{\mathring{\mathscr{B}}_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}&:=\left\|\phi(|h|^{-1})\left\|\mathcal{D}_h^LP(x)\right\|_{L_p(w)}\right\|_{L_q\left(\mathbb{R}^d;\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{|h|^d}\right)}\\
&\geq \left\|\phi(|h|^{-1})\left\|\mathcal{D}_{r\sigma}^LP(x)\right\|_{L_p(E_1;w\mathrm{d}x)}\right\|_{L_q\left(E_2\times [R,\infty);\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{|h|^d}\right)}\\
&\gtrsim\left(w(E_1)\right)^{1/p} \left\|\phi(r^{-1})r^M\right\|_{L_q\left([R,\infty);\frac{\mathrm{d}r}{r}\right)}\,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Since $\phi\in\mathcal{I}_o(0,L)$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that for any $r\in [R,\infty)$, $r^M\phi(r^{-1})\geq r^L\phi(r^{-1})\gtrsim r^{\epsilon}$ (see \eqref{w scaling}).
In addition, $w(E_1)>0$ because $w>0$ a.e. on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
Therefore, the last term in \eqref{230714725} is infinite.
The proof is completed.

body_md:
By \cite[Proposition A.3]{CLSW2023trace},
    $$
    (H_p^2(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x),L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x))_{\widetilde{W}_{\alpha},q}=B_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x),
    $$
    where $(H_p^2(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x),L_p(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x))_{\widetilde{W}_{\alpha},q}$ is the generalized interpolation space (for definition, see \cite[Section 3]{CLSW2023trace}).
First, we choose 
    $$
    v\in L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;H_p^2(w))\quad \text{and}\quad g\in L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))
    $$
    such that
    $$
    \begin{cases}
        \partial_t^{\alpha}v(t,x)=g(t,x),\quad &(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_+\times\mathbb{R}^d,\\
        v(0,x)=u_0(x),\quad &x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
    \end{cases}
    $$
    with the estimate
    \begin{align}   
    \label{23.08.08.17.17}    \|v\|_{L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;H_p^2(w))}+\|g\|_{L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\lesssim \|u_0\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(\mathbb{R}^d,w\,\mathrm{d}x)}.
    \end{align}
    The existence of $v$ and $g$ is established in \cite[Theorem 1.4]{CLSW2023trace}. By \cite[Theorem 2.2]{Dong_Kim2021}, there exists a unique solution $\tilde{v}\in L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;H_p^2(w))$ such that
    $$
    \begin{cases}
        \partial_t^{\alpha}\tilde{v}(t,x)=\Delta \tilde{v}(t,x) +(\Delta v(t,x)-g(t,x)),\quad &(t,x)\in (0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d,\\
        \tilde{v}(0,x)=0,\quad &x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
    \end{cases}
    $$
    with the estimate
    \begin{align}
        \label{23.08.08.17.21}
\||\tilde{v}|+|\tilde{v}_{xx}|+|\partial_t^{\alpha}\tilde{v}|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\lesssim \||\Delta v|+|g|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}.
    \end{align}
    If we put $u:=v+\tilde{v}$, then $u$ is a solution of \eqref{23.05.29.13.09} satisfying \eqref{23.05.29.13.11}.
    Therefore, \eqref{23.08.08.17.17}, \eqref{23.08.08.17.21} and Theorem \ref{thm_lp_diff_equiv} yield that
    \begin{align*}
    \||u|+|u_{xx}|+|\partial_t^{\alpha}u|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}&\lesssim \||\tilde{v}|+|\tilde{v}_{xx}|+|\partial_t^{\alpha}\tilde{v}|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\\
    &\quad +\|v|+|v_{xx}|+|\partial_t^{\alpha}v|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\\
        &\lesssim \||v|+|v_{xx}|+|g|\|_{L_q((0,T),\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\\
        &\lesssim \|v\|_{L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;H_p^2(w))}+\|g\|_{L_q(\mathbb{R}_+,\tilde{w}\,\mathrm{d}t;L_p(w))}\\
        &\lesssim \|u_0\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}\simeq\|u_0\|_{\mathscr{B}_{p,q}^{\phi}(w)}.
    \end{align*}
The uniqueness follows from \cite[Theorem 2.2]{Dong_Kim2021}. The theorem is proved.

    Let $p,q\in[1,\infty)$. Suppose that
    $$
    \tilde{\phi}_p(\lambda):=\frac{\phi(\lambda)}{\lambda^{\frac{d}{p}}}\in\mathcal{I}_o(0,M),
    $$
    for some $M>0$. Then
$$
\|f\|_{C^{\tilde{\phi}_p}_L}\lesssim \|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}},
$$
where

    \|f\|_{C^{\tilde{\phi}_p}_L}:=\|f\|_{L_{\infty}}+\sup_{|h|\leq1}\tilde{\phi}_p(|h|^{-1})\|\mathcal{D}_{h}^Lf\|_{L_{\infty}},\quad L\geq M.

title: Proof
body_md:
By H\"older's inequality,
\begin{align*}
    |\Delta_jf(x)|&\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|\psi_{2^{j-1}}(x-y)+\psi_{2^{j}}(x-y)+\psi_{2^{j+1}}(x-y)||\Delta_jf(y)|\mathrm{d}y\\
    &\leq \sum_{i=-1}^{1}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p}\|\psi_{2^{j+i}}\|_{L_{p'}}=C2^{jd/p}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p},\quad \forall p\in[1,\infty],
\end{align*}
where $1/p+1/p'=1$. This implies that
$$
\sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^{j})2^{-jd/p}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_{\infty}}\lesssim \left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\phi(2^{j})^{\tilde{q}}\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p}^{\tilde{q}}\right)^{1/\tilde{q}},\quad \forall p,\tilde{q}\in[1,\infty).
$$
Similarly, we have
$$
\|S_0f\|_{L_{\infty}}\lesssim \|S_0f\|_{L_p},\quad \forall p\in[1,\infty].
$$
Therefore
$$
\|f\|_{B_{\infty,\infty}^{\tilde{\phi}_p}}\lesssim \|f\|_{B_{p,\tilde{q}}^{\phi}}.
$$
Since $\tilde{\phi}_p\in\mathcal{I}_o(0,M)$, by Theorem \ref{thm_lp_diff_equiv}, we have
$$
\|f\|_{B_{\infty,\infty}^{\tilde{\phi}_p}}\simeq \|f\|_{L_{\infty}}+\sup_{|h|\leq 1}\tilde{\phi}_p(|h|^{-1})\|\mathcal{D}_{h}^Lf\|_{L_{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)}=\|f\|_{C^{\tilde{\phi}_p}_L}.
$$
The remaining part of the proof focuses on proving
$$
\|f\|_{B_{p,\tilde{q}}^{\phi}}\lesssim \|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}}
$$
for an appropriate $\tilde{q}$.
We divide the proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ Case 1. $p\geq q$.

By taking $\tilde{q}=p$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \|f\|_{B_{p,p}^{\phi}}=\|f\|_{F_{p,p}^{\phi}}.
\end{align*}
Since
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^p|\Delta_jf(x)|^p\leq \left(\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q|\Delta_jf(x)|^q\right)^{p/q},
\end{align*}
it is clear that
$$
\|f\|_{F_{p,p}^{\phi}}\leq \|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}}.
$$

$\bullet$ Case 2. $1\leq p<q$.

By taking $\tilde{q}=q$ and using Minkowski's inequality, we obtain
$$
\left(\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q\|\Delta_jf\|_{L_p}^q\right)^{1/q}\leq \left\|\left(\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\phi(2^j)^q|\Delta_jf|^q\right)^{1/q}\right\|_{L_p},
$$
which implies
$$
\|f\|_{B_{p,q}^{\phi}}\leq \|f\|_{F_{p,q}^{\phi}}.
$$
The theorem is proved.

title: Remark
body_md:
$(i)$ In Theorem \ref{23.03.28.16.27}, if
$$
\phi(\lambda)=\lambda^{\gamma},
$$
then $\tilde{\phi}_p\in \mathcal{I}_o(0,M)$ is equivalent to $\gamma-d/p>0$. Since $F_{p,2}^{\phi}=H_p^{\gamma}$ and
$$
C^{\tilde{\phi}_p}_{1}=C^{\gamma-\frac{d}{p}},\quad 0<\gamma-\frac{d}{p}<1,
$$
Therefore, Theorem \ref{23.03.28.16.27} includes \eqref{classical_embedding}.

$(ii)$ If $\phi$ is a Bernstein function satisfying
\begin{align}
\label{23.03.28.17.04}
    c_0\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\delta_0}\leq \frac{\phi(R)}{\phi(r)} \quad \forall 0<r\leq R<\infty,
\end{align}
for some $c_0,\delta_0>0$, then $\phi\in \mathcal{I}(\delta_0,1)$.
Hence, by Proposition \ref{23.05.25.13.12},
$$
\zeta(\lambda):=\frac{\phi(\lambda^2)^{\gamma/2}}{\lambda^{d/p}}\in \mathcal{I}(\delta_0\gamma-d/p,\gamma-d/p),\quad \gamma>0.
$$
If $\gamma>\frac{d}{\delta_0p}$,
then by Theorem \ref{23.03.28.16.27} and Proposition \ref{23.05.25.13.12},
$$
(1-\phi(\Delta))^{-\gamma/2}L_p=H_p^{\phi,\gamma}\hookrightarrow C^{\zeta}_L,\quad L>\gamma-\frac{d}{p}.
$$
Since for $|h|\leq1$,
\begin{align*}
    \frac{c_0}{|h|^{\delta_0\gamma-\frac{d}{p}}}\leq\frac{\zeta(|h|^{-1})}{\zeta(1)},
\end{align*}
we have
$$
H_p^{\phi,\gamma}\, \hookrightarrow \, C^{\zeta}_L \, \hookrightarrow \, C^{\delta_0\gamma-d/p}.
$$
